title: MCP++ DurableExecutor@1
description: Typed request/result catalog for DurableExecutor@1, plus DurableJournalRecord@1 and CrashRecoveryReceipt@1. Every method has a closed request and result shape. Journaled transitions map to Event DAG event_type values. Finalize binds final outputs to signed ExecutionReceipt@1. Interface: DurableExecutor@1. Normative prose: ipfs_accelerate_py/mcplusplus/docs/architecture/durable-execution.md. Authority: plan KD-12, ADR-0005, MCPP-050.
$comment: Interface labels: DurableExecutor@1, DurableJournalRecord@1, CrashRecoveryReceipt@1. Schema markers: mcp++/durable/executor-request@1, mcp++/durable/executor-result@1, mcp++/durable/journal-record@1, mcp++/durable/crash-recovery-receipt@1. Journal is recovery authority; Event DAG is provenance only.

cid.description: IPFS CID. CIDv1 base32 (b…) preferred for new mints; CIDv0 (Qm…) remains readable when historical.

timestampMs.description: Unix epoch milliseconds (safe integer range). Informational only; not causal authority.

executionId.description: Stable durable execution identity assigned by start.

requestId.description: Caller-supplied id correlating a single method call.

idempotencyKey.description: Idempotency key for externally visible commits and start dedupe.

fencingToken.description: Exclusive-work fencing epoch. Stale tokens MUST be rejected.

terminalStatus.description: Terminal statuses eligible for finalize or cancel completion.

journalTransition.description: Closed journal transition kinds. Each maps to an Event DAG event_type (see eventDagEventType and transitionEventMap).

eventDagEventType.description: Canonical Profile F Event DAG event_type values used when publishing journaled transitions.

transitionEventMap.description: Normative mapping from journal transition to Event DAG event_type. Documented for validators and adapters; not a runtime payload.

ok.description: True when the method call succeeded structurally and was applied (or idempotently replayed).

event_cid.description: Event DAG node CID for the journaled transition when published.

idempotent_replay.description: True when start returned an existing execution for the same idempotency_key.

progress_cid.description: CID of the durable progress document.

durable.description: DurableExecutor@1 timers MUST be durable (survive process death when journaled).

journal_records.description: Optional journal slice when include_journal was true.

execution_id.description: When null/omitted, adapter recovers its recoverable set.

fencing_token.description: Required when reclaiming a specific execution without claim_new_fencing_token.

claim_new_fencing_token.description: When true, advance fencing epoch for exclusive recover.

after_kill.description: Hint that this recover follows process death (gate 17 path).

receipt_cid.description: Optional pre-minted ExecutionReceipt@1 CID. When null, adapter mints and binds.

output_cids.description: Final outputs; MUST match ExecutionResult@1.output_cids and ExecutionReceipt@1.output_cids.

sign_receipt.description: When true (default for cross-trust), receipt MUST carry a non-null signature.

envelope_cid.description: Optional echo of start envelope; MUST match journal root when present.

receipt_cid.description: CID of bound ExecutionReceipt@1. Final outputs bind through this receipt.

signature_present.description: True when the bound ExecutionReceipt@1 carries a non-null signature.

event_type.description: Mapped Profile F event_type for this transition. When set, MUST match the normative transition→event_type table.

receipt_cid.description: When transition is finalized, CID of the bound ExecutionReceipt@1.

parents.description: Prior journal record CIDs (empty for root started).

event_cid.description: Published Event DAG node for this journal transition.

canonicalization.description: Required on new journal record mints.

side_effects_not_replayed.description: Idempotency keys of committed side effects that recover MUST NOT re-apply.

durableDocument.description: Any top-level durable-interface document defined by this schema.
